map.Lessons 2-3, 2-4 & 2-5 — median, box plo: Lessons 2-3, 2-4 & 2-5 — median, box plots, range & IQR. Four gates stand between Rosa and her hearing.
map.Previously: the reader proved Pimm's cen: Last time: the reader showed that Pimm's census questions told us nothing. Distortion level: still rising.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: the crew tore: Last time, in Episode 1: the crew took apart the "official census form." The council noticed. Rosa's permit hearing is now on the calendar.
map.Friday. That's how long we have to show: Friday. That is when we show the council Rosa's REAL numbers.
map.Pimm keeps waving one terrible Tuesday a: Pimm keeps showing one bad Tuesday. One day is not my whole stall!
map.Then we don't show them one day. We show: Then we do not show one day. We show the middle of all her days. It is the number her data centers on.
map.The median is the middle value when the: The median is the middle value when the data is in order. Half the days are at or below it. Half are at or above it.
map.Rosa's notebook. Five market days, five: Rosa's notebook. Five market days. Five visitor counts. Written in churro grease.
map.Raw loot log. But it's shuffled — a midd: The loot log is mixed up. Make the list sorted first. Then find the middle.
map.Sorting protocol: line the counts up sma: Sort the counts from smallest to largest. THEN the middle one, number three of five, is the median. No averaging needed.
map.Reader — sort Rosa's five days and find: Reader, sort Rosa's five days. Find her true middle!
map.Rosa's five market days: 22, 17, 30, 25,: Rosa had 22, 17, 30, 25, 19 visitors on five market days. Sort them in your head or on paper. Then enter the median.
map.Conceptual: the median is the middle of: Conceptual: the median is the middle of the SORTED list. Half the days are below it. Half are above. Always sort first.
Procedural: put them in order: 17, 19, ?, ?, ?. With five values, the median is the 3rd one.
map.If the council won't read a table, they': If the council will not read a table, they will read a BANNER. One box. Five numbers. No lies.
map.It's a box plot. Five numbers tell the w: It is a box plot. Five numbers tell the story: minimum, quartile 1, median, quartile 3, maximum. The box has the middle half of the data.
map.Q1 is the median of the lower half; Q3 i: Q1 is the median of the lower half. Q3 is the median of the upper half. The box goes from Q1 to Q3.
map.Paint the three missing marks on the ban: Paint the three missing marks on the banner: Q1, median, Q3!
map.The co-op's seven recorded crowds, alrea: The co-op counted seven crowds. They are sorted: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20. The whiskers are painted (min 4, max 20). Enter the three missing marks.
map.Conceptual: the median splits the sorted: Conceptual: the median splits the sorted list in half. Q1 is the median of the LOWER half. Q3 is the median of the UPPER half.
map.Procedural: 7 values → median is the 4th: Procedural: 7 values, so the median is the 4th. Lower half: 4, 7, 9 (middle: ?). Upper half: 13, 16, 20 (middle: ?).
He is using the range: max minus min. Just two numbers. The two oddest ones.
map.Counter-protocol: the IQR — Q3 minus Q1: Our answer: the IQR, Q3 minus Q1. It shows how spread out the middle half is. Outliers cannot change it. It is the honest width.
map.Range = max − min (fragile). IQR = Q3 −: Range = max − min (easy to break). IQR = Q3 − Q1 (strong). Same data, very different stories.
map.Compute both widths, reader. Let's see w: Find both widths, reader. Which one is Pimm hiding behind?
map.Same data: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20 (Q1 =: Same data: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20 (Q1 = 7, Q3 = 16). Pimm uses one width. The crew uses the other. Find both.
map.Conceptual: range uses the two END value: Conceptual: range uses the two END values, the biggest and smallest days. IQR uses the box edges, the steady middle half.
map.Thursday night. A new poster appears on: Thursday night. A new poster is on the council board. It has four numbers and no middle.
map.Ha! He thinks an even count breaks the m: Ha! He thinks an even count breaks the median. Boss fight!
map.When two values share the middle, the me: When two values share the middle, the median is the number halfway between them. Add the two middles. Cut the total in half. The middle of everything.
map.Tomorrow we hand the council the middle: Tomorrow we give the council the middle AND the width. Tonight, we solve Pimm's even-count puzzle.
map.Reader takes this one. Banner's already: Reader takes this one. The banner is painted. Do not make me redo it.
map.Boss Gate: find the median of an even-co: Boss Gate: find the median of an even-count data set. Then say what a small IQR proves.
map.BOSS GATE. Two locks. Pimm's \"no median: BOSS GATE. Two locks. Pimm's "no median" claim stops here.
map.Pimm's \"audit\" lists four days: 8, 10,: Pimm's "audit" has four days: 8, 10, 14, 18. He says an even count has NO median. Two locks:
map.Rosa's box plot shows a small IQR huggin: Rosa's box plot has a small IQR close to her median. At the hearing, that PROVES:
map.Conceptual: with an even count, TWO valu: Conceptual: with an even count, TWO values share the middle. The median is the value halfway between them. Add them, then split the sum evenly.
map.Median 22, box snug around the middle… m: Median 22, and the box is tight around the middle. My stall looks as steady as it feels.
map.Friday: payout day. Pimm \"rounds\" ever: Friday is payout day. Pimm "rounds" each vendor's share. Guess who checks his division?
map.Median.Sort first. The middle value of a: Median.Sort first. With an odd count, the median is the middle number. With an even count, it is halfway between the two middles.
map.Box plot.Five numbers — min, Q1, median,: Box plot.Five numbers: min, Q1, median, Q3, max. The box holds the middle half of the data.
map.Range.Max minus min. Easy to compute, ea: Range.Max minus min. Easy to find, but one odd day can ruin it.
IQR.Q3 minus Q1, the width of the box. Outliers cannot change it.
map.completed Unit 2 · Episode 2: The Middle: finished Unit 2 · Episode 2: The Middle of Everything and showed they know medians, box plots, range, and interquartile range.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.IQR = 10 − 6 = 4. Big range, small IQR →: IQR = 10 − 6 = 4. Big range, small IQR: the middle is calm. The edges are odd days.
map.Median = (9 + 13) ÷ 2 = 11. Even counts: Median = (9 + 13) ÷ 2 = 11. Even counts do have medians. They hide a bit.
map.17, 19, 22, 25, 30 — the middle is 22. R: 17, 19, 22, 25, 30: the middle is 22. Rosa's usual day, proven.
map.30 is the middle of the UNSORTED list. S: 30 is the middle of the UNSORTED list. Sort first. Order matters a lot.
map.Line the five counts up smallest to larg: Put the five counts in order, smallest to largest. Take the one in position three.
map.Box from 7 to 16, line at 11 — the banne: Box from 7 to 16, line at 11. The banner is done. The middle half shows.
map.Split the sorted list: median is the 4th: Split the sorted list. The median is the 4th of 7. Then find the middle of each half.
map.Range 16 — but IQR only 9. Pimm quoted t: Range 16, but IQR only 9. Pimm used the wild days. The box tells the calm truth.
map.IQR is the box width: Q3 minus Q1 — chec: IQR is the box width: Q3 minus Q1. Check the Gate 2 marks.
map.Lock 1 holds. Find the two middle values: Lock 1 is still shut. Find the two middle values first. Then go halfway between them.
map.Lock 2 holds. A small IQR says the middl: Lock 2 is still shut. A small IQR says the middle half of the days are CLOSE TOGETHER. What does that mean for Rosa?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Median 12 — even counts: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Median 12. Even counts can't hide. A tight box means steady crowds. See you at the hearing, Pimm.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
